subject: Cerebro Health — implementation kickoff & model/size recommendations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cerebro.health
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cerebro Health onboarding — model shortlist + traffic snapshot (kickoff)

Hey Jordan / Ben,

Looping you in for implementation planning on the Cerebro Health engagement (incoming production integration next quarter). Quick summary up front and a couple of asks so we can lock the kickoff agenda.

High level: Cerebro is building an AI assistant for clinicians to summarize patient visit notes and flag follow-up tasks. They care about accuracy on clinical language, 8k context for multi-note summaries, and predictable per-request latency under 600ms for the majority of requests.

What CS collected (attached):
- Model shortlist: Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp16), Llama-2-13B-chat (q4_0), Redmond-v1-7B (customer preferred open model), and a small GPT-x-4-compatible baseline for canary tests.
- Context need: typical request concatenates 3 notes, median context ~5.5k tokens, peak ~8.5k tokens (they asked for 8k target, vendor samples show some slightly longer turns).
- Usage: 800 monthly active clinicians, expected adoption ramp to 2k MAU in 6 months. Peak concurrent editors estimated at 30 during morning triage.
- Token profile (see attached spreadsheet): avg prompt tokens 240, avg generation tokens 130, tail 95th gen tokens ~750 for long summaries.

Primary asks for you two before the kickoff:
1) Confirm feasibility of serving Llama-2-13B-chat and Mistral-INSTRUCT concurrently with 8k context — recommended initial instance types, starting GPU count for canary (targeting 500 MAU equivalent traffic), and safe SLOs we can promise.
2) Any immediate red flags on the token profile vs. cost — do we want to propose a mild generation cap at 1k tokens or recommend server-side chunking/summary pipelines?
3) Schedule: can we propose a Monday 5/30 10:00 PT kickoff with Cerebro?

I'll be on the kickoff and will coordinate procurement + legal for the SOW signatures (attached). Procurement contact is procurement@cerebro.health (cc'd).

Thanks — quick replies appreciated so I can include your notes in the kickoff deck.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: Cerebro_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: cerebro_token_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@cerebro.health
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cerebro Health onboarding — model shortlist + traffic snapshot (kickoff)

Thanks Marissa — quick read and a few clarifying Qs inline.

Marissa,
- Model shortlist: fine to include all three as variants. For the 8k context target: Llama-2-13B-chat will need kv-cache planning (we can run with sequence splitting and KV spill thresholds), Mistral-7B should be OK with 8k if we run fp16 on A100-class or H100 with optimized kernels. Redmond-v1-7B (their preference) is likely the cheapest but we need to verify quality on clinical language; recommend we include a short eval sweep prior to production.

Ben, can you sanity-check the below initial capacity?
- Canary target: sized for ~500 MAU burst profile (peak concurrency 20)
  - Option A (latency-first): 2x H100-80GB with model parallelism for Llama-13B; 4x for mixed variants if we want headroom.
  - Option B (cost-first): 4x A100-40GB (q4_0 for Llama-13B), may increase tail latency but saves ~30% on unit cost.

On tokens: their 95th gen token ~750 is concerning for cost. Suggest we offer two mitigations:
1) Server-side chunking + hierarchical summarization pipeline for very long notes (reduces average generation length)
2) Soft generation cap of 1k tokens with an explicit fallback summary flow if clinicians request a full verbatim extraction.

Scheduling: 5/30 10:00 PT works for me.

Also — do we have a quick eval harness for clinical accuracy on Redmond-v1? If not, I'll coordinate with Research to run a 200-sample medical notes pass.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com

From: Emma Li <emma@cerebro.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cerebro Health onboarding — model shortlist + traffic snapshot (kickoff)

Hi Marissa / Jordan — thanks for the concise summary. Answering Jordan's clarifying questions below. Forwarding their procurement team if needed.

- Prompt/generation sizes: Our internal telemetry (sample of 6k visits) shows median prompt ~250 tokens and median generation ~120 tokens. The 95th generation token ~750 is accurate for multi-note summaries when clinicians ask for expanded detail — that is rare (~2% of sessions).
- Concurrency and MAU: Peak concurrent human editors: 28–32 during morning triage. MAU target is indeed 2k in 6 months.
- Redmond-v1: we ran a small pilot. It performs well on entity extraction but struggles with some structured template language — we can share a small eval corpus.

Links:
- Sample dataset (de-identified): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cerebro-samples
- Procurement SOW / DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/DS-cc-7893

We can do 5/30 10:00 PT for kickoff. For the canary, procurement prefers a predictable committed starting configuration. Happy to review your capacity options in the meeting.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Head of Product, Cerebro Health
emma@cerebro.health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Li <emma@cerebro.health>
Cc: procurement@cerebro.health
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Cerebro Health onboarding — model shortlist + traffic snapshot (kickoff)

Appreciate the quick answers, Emma — helpful. Wrapping up our internal pre-kickoff notes so the kickoff deck is actionable. Plan below (we'll present this and confirm on 5/30):

1) Model plan (canary -> prod):
   - Canary: Redmond-v1-7B (to validate integration and perf), Mistral-INSTRUCT-7B as a parallel variant for quality comparison. Limit canary scope to a 10% clinician cohort (approx 80 users) and traffic baseline of 500 MAU equivalent.
   - Production roll: Llama-2-13B-chat as primary for latency-critical flows; Redmond-v1 and Mistral as lower-cost or fallback variants.

2) Capacity recommendation (initial committed config for procurement):
   - Start with 3x A100-80GB nodes (q4_0 for Llama-13B) to provide a balance of cost and latency; autoscale policy for burst to H100 nodes if SLOs deteriorate. This should handle typical daily peak with safety headroom for early growth.

3) Token and cost mitigations:
   - Implement server-side chunking for >4k context and a hierarchical summarizer to reduce average generation length.
   - Soft cap at 1k generation tokens with explicit UI messaging.

4) Next steps before kickoff:
   - Marissa: confirm procurement preferred committed config and SOW signatory.
   - Emma: share the 200-sample eval corpus for Redmond check (link received).
   - Ben: prepare a short perf-run doc with expected latencies for A100 q4_0 vs H100 fp16 for 8k context.
   - Jordan: coordinate short clinical eval with Research if needed.

I'll include these in the kickoff deck and bring a short capacity/scale diagram. See the HubSpot deal and Drive folder for artifacts.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
